- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video and may request to speak using the

the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's

MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  DECEMBER 15, 2021

CHAIR STEGURA called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates to order at 7:05 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Stegura, Bain, O’Malley, Radocchio, Uppal, Wisot

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Bacinski, Chan-Southwell, Larson, Schachter,
  Yoo (alternate)

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING, OCTOBER 27,
  2021

COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
RADOCCHIO to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 27, 2021

There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

CHAIR STEGURA thanked Committee Member Wisot and Committee Member Chan-Southwell
for their service to the city.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210363 - DRAFT GENERAL PLAN 2040 AND DRAFT
  PROGRAM ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (PEIR) - DRAFT SUSTAINABILITY
  ELEMENT

Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation on the Draft Sustainability Element.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN asked about the data being used. For example, the energy
reduction measurements are from 2018. Due to the pandemic, residential energy must be up and
asked is there is a way to obtain more recent data.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that these long-term plans take time to put together and at
the time, the consultants used the most recent data available. In the future, staff will monitor the
energy usage data and adjust goals accordingly. In terms of greenhouse gas emissions, it’s been
quite some time since a community-wide inventory has been done. The SBCCOG will be working
on updating the community-wide inventories in the next few months. Planning Manager Naughton
stated that language can be added to the implementation measures to require updating the
analysis.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN inquired about encouraging residential solar. Planning Manager
Naughton stated that the document does detail the energy mix that both SCE and CPA contain.
CHAIR STEGURA stated that Energy Policy ENG 9-1-9 speaks about educating the public on
sustainable means of lowering energy cost and sustainable building practices.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN suggested providing residents with a resource within the city to
provide more information on residential solar.

Planning Manager Naughton shared Policy No.ENG 9-2-4 – Promote the application of active
solar energy systems in residential development by facilitating, where possible, the efforts of
federal and state entities in the allocation of cost incentive programs.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 15, 2021
 After a brief discussion, the policy language remained unchanged.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN asked about the goal regarding water resources used by golf
courses and the recycling of water for these facilities and asked why this goal is to do this by
2030. Planning Manager Naughton stated that there is no purple pipe on the Peninsula. The
closest purple pipe will be in 2022 to the Palos Verdes Golf Course. Currently there are no plans
for extensions of purple pipe. COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN asked who would make the decisions
for purple pipe. Planning Manager Naughton stated that this would be a public works decision
and it would require improvements of rights-of-way of several entities.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Rolling Hills Golf Course has a natural aquifer on site
that they use to water the golf course.

Planning Manager Naughton referenced Policy No. 9-2-3. COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN
suggested changing “cooperate” to “prioritize”. COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT agreed with this
change. There was no objection by the committee and a recommendation to make this change
will be recommended to the Planning Commission.

CHAIR STEGURA stated that in regards to incentives, staff is always looking for grants and
programs to incentivize the for greener measures.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN suggested working with private industry to allow them to offer
discounts for residents.

COMMITTEE MEMBER O’MALLEY stated that one of the challenges with solar is that there are
so many companies. General education on the process would be helpful.

COMMITTEE MEMBER O’MALLEY stated that in regards to the air monitoring station, there are
specific technical reasons for their location. There is an Annual Plan and comments can be
provided; information on the next Annual Plan Update will be provided to staff. COMMITTEE
MEMBER O’MALLEY stated that SCAQMD received grants and has been deploying low-cost
centers that expanded the network. There is a SCAQMD app or visit the SCAQMD website. If
additional federal funding comes through, there is funding to improve the air monitoring networks
nationwide.

COMMITTEE MEMBER O’MALLEY stated that she agrees with the water use and understands
the challenges. She stated that the Hyperion Plant cleans water and then dumps it into the ocean;
she suggested looking into the possibility of capturing this water to use for the South Bay
communities.

CHAIR STEGURA stated that city permitting processes should be more resident friendly for solar
roofs or compliant roof tiles and provide a wider selection.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN inquired about what the community does to interface with beach
cities that are in the process of planning for sea level rise. Planning Manager Naughton stated
that staff meets in a regional group with Community Development Directors regarding short-range
and long-range plans. When it comes to adaptation planning, SBCCOG did vulnerability
assessments and there were no impacts in regards to threats to the city for sea level rise. The
results of the city’s vulnerability assessment were specific to wildfire and extreme heat events and
a lot of the implementation measures in the adaptation plan are about addressing those threats.
Although the city is not directly affected by sea level rise, the city will have cascading affects from
adjacent cities but discussion on secondary affects have not begun.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN expressed her concern with traffic in the case of a major weather
event that may affect surrounding cities and stated that the City will be equally impacted.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL, Planning Manager Naughton stated
that there are items that the City are already working on. Adopting these as formal goals, gives
the City a plan for short-term and long-term action. A lot of the policies and implementation
measures are new and a lot are aspirational since the City does not have the funding or staff
resources in order to achieve them. Progress will be able to be measured by looking back at this
document to see if the City has met these goals.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN, Planning Manager Naughton stated
that the first step will be to map out the short term and long-term goals and set-up a review on an
annual basis.

COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT commended staff and the committee for creating a thorough and
realistic plan which will continue to make this City a great place to live.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 15, 2021
 Planning Manager Naughton stated that she welcomes any comments or questions after this
meeting. The Planning Commission agenda for the meeting of January 10, 2022 will be finalized
on January 6, 2022.

NONE
